# US launches task force to disrupt Iran's land-based supply routes
By Al Jazeera Staff

The United States military's Central Command (CENTCOM) has announced a plan to block Iran's land-based supply routes, expanding its months-long naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz.

CENTCOM, which oversees US military operations in the Middle East, announced on Saturday that it had established a new task force "to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials".

Task Force Iron Gate will reinforce "the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea", CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said.

Based in Tampa, Florida, the task force will coordinate with other US government agencies on preventing weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Michael Mulroy, a former US deputy assistant defence secretary for the Middle East, told Al Jazeera the task force will identify where "weapons systems are coming in, how they could potentially be cut off".

He added that future escalation will likely target "economic and infrastructure targets, as part of this comprehensive plan to cut the regime off."

CENTCOM separately said on Saturday that it had disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman. A US military aircraft fired on the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda after directing the crew to abandon targeted spaces.

"Enforcement actions since July have resulted in U.S. forces redirecting 147 commercial vessels that complied", and disabling "five merchant ships that refused to comply".

On Saturday, Iran's official news agency IRNA reported explosions on Qeshm Island and in cities including Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy reported that two oil tankers struck mines near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, with the vessels suffering "severe damage" after hitting the mines.
